theory.intro: Dotting a vector with itself gives the square of its length. That link turns a length question into a dot product question, and it lets you expand brackets such as $|\underset{\sim}{a}+\underset{\sim}{b}|^{2}$.
facts: $\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{a}=|\underset{\sim}{a}|^{2}$. A non-zero vector makes an angle of $0^{\circ}$ with itself. The identity also holds for the zero vector, although its angle is undefined.
In components it is the usual length rule: $\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{a}=a_{1}^{2}+a_{2}^{2}$.
Dot products expand like brackets, so $|\underset{\sim}{a}+\underset{\sim}{b}|^{2}=|\underset{\sim}{a}|^{2}+2\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b}+|\underset{\sim}{b}|^{2}$.
Changing the sign changes only the middle term: $|\underset{\sim}{a}-\underset{\sim}{b}|^{2}=|\underset{\sim}{a}|^{2}-2\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b}+|\underset{\sim}{b}|^{2}$.

For two non-zero vectors, the cross term $2\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b}$ is zero exactly when the vectors are perpendicular. The zero vector has dot product zero with every vector, although it has no defined angle.
Lengths do not simply add, so $|\underset{\sim}{a}+\underset{\sim}{b}|\ne|\underset{\sim}{a}|+|\underset{\sim}{b}|$ in general.
steps: Replace each self dot product with a squared magnitude
Substitute the known values and evaluate

workedExamples.question_text:
Find the self dot product in each case.

(a) $\underset{\sim}{u}=\begin{pmatrix}-5\\8\end{pmatrix}$.

(b) $\underset{\sim}{v}=\begin{pmatrix}3\\-4\\6\end{pmatrix}$.

Find $\underset{\sim}{v}\cdot\underset{\sim}{v}$ and verify that it equals $|\underset{\sim}{v}|^{2}$ in each case.

(a) $\underset{\sim}{v}=(t-4)\underset{\sim}{i}+(2t+2)\underset{\sim}{j}$.

(b) $\underset{\sim}{v}=(\sqrt{6}+\sqrt{2})\underset{\sim}{i}+(\sqrt{6}-\sqrt{2})\underset{\sim}{j}$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) $\begin{aligned}\underset{\sim}{v}\cdot\underset{\sim}{v}&=(t-4)^{2}+(2t+2)^{2}\\&=t^{2}-8t+16+4t^{2}+8t+4\\&=5t^{2}+20\end{aligned}$

$|\underset{\sim}{v}|^{2}=(t-4)^{2}+(2t+2)^{2}=5t^{2}+20$.

Both sides equal $5t^{2}+20$.

(b) $\begin{aligned}\underset{\sim}{v}\cdot\underset{\sim}{v}&=(\sqrt{6}+\sqrt{2})^{2}+(\sqrt{6}-\sqrt{2})^{2}\\&=8+4\sqrt{3}+8-4\sqrt{3}\\&=16\end{aligned}$

$|\underset{\sim}{v}|=\sqrt{16}=4$, so $|\underset{\sim}{v}|^{2}=16$.

Both sides equal $16$.

workedExamples.question_text:
The vectors $\underset{\sim}{p}$ and $\underset{\sim}{q}$ have equal magnitudes.

(a) Show that $\underset{\sim}{p}\cdot\underset{\sim}{p}=\underset{\sim}{q}\cdot\underset{\sim}{q}$.

(b) Hence show that $(\underset{\sim}{p}+\underset{\sim}{q})\cdot(\underset{\sim}{p}-\underset{\sim}{q})=0$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Squaring the equal magnitudes gives $|\underset{\sim}{p}|^{2}=|\underset{\sim}{q}|^{2}$.

Using the self-dot property, $\underset{\sim}{p}\cdot\underset{\sim}{p}=\underset{\sim}{q}\cdot\underset{\sim}{q}$.

(b) $\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}(\underset{\sim}{p}+\underset{\sim}{q})\cdot(\underset{\sim}{p}-\underset{\sim}{q})\\&=\underset{\sim}{p}\cdot\underset{\sim}{p}-\underset{\sim}{p}\cdot\underset{\sim}{q}+\underset{\sim}{q}\cdot\underset{\sim}{p}-\underset{\sim}{q}\cdot\underset{\sim}{q}\\&=|\underset{\sim}{p}|^{2}-|\underset{\sim}{q}|^{2}\\&=0\end{aligned}$

The cross terms cancel because the dot product is commutative.

workedExamples.question_text:
Find the exact magnitude of $\underset{\sim}{a}+\underset{\sim}{b}$ in each case.

(a) The vectors are perpendicular, with $|\underset{\sim}{a}|=9$ and $|\underset{\sim}{b}|=12$.

(b) $|\underset{\sim}{a}|=6$, $|\underset{\sim}{b}|=5$, and the angle between them is $60^{\circ}$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Expand the self dot product:

$\begin{aligned}|\underset{\sim}{a}+\underset{\sim}{b}|^{2}&=(\underset{\sim}{a}+\underset{\sim}{b})\cdot(\underset{\sim}{a}+\underset{\sim}{b})\\&=|\underset{\sim}{a}|^{2}+2\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b}+|\underset{\sim}{b}|^{2}\end{aligned}$

(a) Perpendicular vectors have $\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b}=0$.

$\begin{aligned}|\underset{\sim}{a}+\underset{\sim}{b}|^{2}&=9^{2}+2(0)+12^{2}\\&=225\\|\underset{\sim}{a}+\underset{\sim}{b}|&=\sqrt{225}\\&=15\end{aligned}$

(b) $\begin{aligned}\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b}&=(6)(5)\cos60^{\circ}\\&=15\\|\underset{\sim}{a}+\underset{\sim}{b}|^{2}&=6^{2}+2(15)+5^{2}\\&=91\\|\underset{\sim}{a}+\underset{\sim}{b}|&=\sqrt{91}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: Given that $|\underset{\sim}{a}+\underset{\sim}{b}|=|\underset{\sim}{a}-\underset{\sim}{b}|$, use the self-dot property to prove that $\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b}=0$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Square both sides and apply the self-dot property:

$\begin{aligned}|\underset{\sim}{a}+\underset{\sim}{b}|^{2}&=|\underset{\sim}{a}-\underset{\sim}{b}|^{2}\\(\underset{\sim}{a}+\underset{\sim}{b})\cdot(\underset{\sim}{a}+\underset{\sim}{b})&=(\underset{\sim}{a}-\underset{\sim}{b})\cdot(\underset{\sim}{a}-\underset{\sim}{b})\\|\underset{\sim}{a}|^{2}+2\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b}+|\underset{\sim}{b}|^{2}&=|\underset{\sim}{a}|^{2}-2\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b}+|\underset{\sim}{b}|^{2}\\4\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b}&=0\\\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b}&=0\end{aligned}$
